name: Times club monthly special crossword No 20,279

solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sheep-faced figure hit in the jaw by boxing reprobate, nursing mouth

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, as a box holds its contents, so one piece wraps around another
a nurse holds a baby in her arms, so the reprobate wraps around the next piece

blocks.note: to chin someone is to hit them on the chin
a rip is a dissolute, worthless person
os is the Latin word for mouth, used in anatomy
by as in multiplication, three by four, written with the times sign

explanation.surface: A boxer is knocked on the jaw by a villainous opponent who is guarding his mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: The boxing match is a decoy: 'boxing' and 'nursing' both mean holding inside. 'By' gives X as in the multiplication sign, three by four.
explanation.definitionFit: A criosphinx is an Egyptian sphinx carved with a ram's head instead of a human one.

clue.text: Compare curbs attached to online forum

indicators.note: to curb something is to hold it in check, so the compare abbreviation holds the next piece

blocks.note: cf. is the abbreviation for the Latin confer, meaning compare
on as in switched on or connected

explanation.surface: Comparing restrictions placed on an internet discussion board.
explanation.definitionFit: Conf is a short form of conference, used for a discussion group on an online bulletin board.

clue.text: Around House of Lords area, I ignore sound of German

indicators.note: around places one piece on either side of the other, enclosing it

blocks.note: I cut, as in cutting someone dead in the street
HL is the standard abbreviation for the House of Lords
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Someone at Westminster ignores the way German is spoken.
explanation.walkthrough: I CUT wraps around HL and A. Cutting someone is pointedly ignoring them.
explanation.definitionFit: The ich-laut is the soft German consonant heard in 'ich', a palatal fricative made near the front of the mouth.

clue.text: Swindler keeps breaking law and a mark, unknown, traps employee after vacating suit in S Asia

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold on to it, so the swindler holds the next piece
something broken is smashed up, and its pieces fall into a new order
a trap closes around its catch, so these pieces enclose the employee's letters
vacating empties a place, leaving only its walls, so only the outside of the word survives

blocks.note: a shark is a swindler or con man
taken as written, before being rearranged
taken as written
M for mark, the old German currency
the first and last letters of employee
z is an algebraic unknown, like x and y

explanation.surface: A con man breaks the law and nabs a worker after he leaves, in a story set in South Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: SHARK holds a shuffled LAW to give SHALWAR; A, M and Z hold EE to give KAMEEZ.
explanation.definitionFit: The shalwar kameez is the loose trousers and long tunic outfit worn across Pakistan, India and neighbouring countries.

clue.text: Henry after Saudi money

blocks.note: Hal is a familiar form of Henry, as for Shakespeare's Prince Hal
à la, French for in the manner of or after

explanation.surface: Prince Henry follows the money to Saudi Arabia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' looks like a placing instruction, but it supplies letters of its own: à la means 'after the fashion of'.
explanation.definitionFit: The halala is a coin of Saudi Arabia, a hundredth part of the riyal.

clue.text: Currently votes against preserving old stuff

indicators.note: preserving keeps something safe inside, so the votes hold the next piece

blocks.note: nays are votes against a motion
O is the abbreviation for old
to wad is to stuff or pad

explanation.surface: These days the votes go against keeping antiques.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean at the present time, in the modern day, as opposed to formerly.

clue.text: A helping of baba ghanoush in an Indian garden

indicators.note: a helping is a portion served from a larger dish, so the letters are a part of the phrase

blocks.note: found across the two words of the dish's name

explanation.surface: Someone eats a portion of aubergine dip while sitting in a garden in India.
explanation.walkthrough: Baba ghanoush is a Middle Eastern dip made from smoked aubergine.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagh is the Hindi and Urdu word for a garden or orchard, used in Indian place names.

clue.text: Legal expert has an interrogation shortened under uneducated Australian bloke

indicators.note: something shortened has had its end cut off, so the final letter goes
in a down answer, under places the following letters below the bloke's name in the column

blocks.note: Alf is Australian slang for an uncouth, uneducated man
the indefinite article
a quiz is a questioning

explanation.surface: A lawyer is grilled, not for long, by a rough Aussie.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'under' places the A and QUI below ALF.
explanation.definitionFit: An alfaqui is a Muslim scholar learned in religious law, an expounder of the Koran.

clue.text: I’m very annoyed the man’s going to cheat Society, collecting billions

indicators.note: collecting gathers something in, so the cheating word takes in the next piece

blocks.note: he'll, short for he will
a sell is a swindle, and to sell someone is to cheat them
B is the abbreviation for billion
S is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: Someone fumes that a man plans to defraud a society of billions.
explanation.walkthrough: B sits inside SELL after its first letter, and the S for Society follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Hell's bells is a mild exclamation of exasperation, used when someone is irritated.

clue.text: Central American roaming Lithuania but never India

indicators.note: roaming means wandering about, so the letters drift into a new order
never means not ever, so every occurrence of the letter is left out

blocks.note: taken as written
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A traveller from Central America wanders through Lithuania but never visits India.
explanation.walkthrough: Both I's go from Lithuania, and the seven letters left are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Nahuatl is the language of the Aztecs and their modern descendants in Mexico, so it is a Central American language and people.

clue.text: Plenty of Scots more enthusiastic to roll up, regularly expressing resistance

definitions.note: a Scots word, so 'of Scots' says whose language it is

indicators.note: expressing means squeezing out, and regularly says it happens at even intervals along the letters

blocks.note: warmer as in more ardent
to furl a flag or sail is to roll it up
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Scots arrive in numbers, keener to turn up and show their opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: In WARMERFURL every third letter is an R; squeezing out all three leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Wameful is Scots for a bellyful, the wame being the belly, so a large quantity.

clue.text: I did America, wandering round Maine; she was in charge of France

definitions.text: she was in charge of France

indicators.note: wandering means straying from a set path, so the letters stray into a new order
round places the rearranged letters on both sides of the state abbreviation

blocks.note: taken as written, before being rearranged
ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine

explanation.surface: A traveller boasts of touring America and taking in Maine, then turns to a woman who once ruled France.
explanation.definitionFit: Marie de' Medici governed France as regent for her young son Louis XIII after Henri IV was assassinated in 1610.

clue.text: Reprobate turned violent, an act exposing British king

indicators.note: turned means turned round, so the following words are read from the end

blocks.note: a cad is a man who behaves dishonourably
red as in bloody, marked by violence, as in red in tooth and claw
the indefinite article
an act of parliament is a law

explanation.surface: A scoundrel turns nasty, and his deed reveals a king of Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned violent' reads as a single phrase, but 'turned' governs everything after it up to 'exposing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadwalader was a seventh-century king of the Britons in Wales, remembered as the last British king.

clue.text: Life forces pizza topping from one’s mouth?

indicators.note: what comes from a mouth is speech, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: the classic pizza topping, said aloud

explanation.surface: A comic image of pizza topping sliding out of someone's mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: Qi is pronounced 'chee', so its plural with the s sounds like the topping.
explanation.definitionFit: In Chinese philosophy qi is the vital energy that flows through every living thing, so its plural is life forces.

clue.text: Presumably the person in charge of steak for large lizard

blocks.note: surface padding that owns up to the joke: the name is being read as if it described someone's job
chuck is a cut of beef from the neck and shoulder
a walla or wallah is the person in charge of a particular thing, from Hindi

explanation.surface: Someone muses on who must be responsible for the steak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Presumably' admits the joke: the lizard's name is read as if it meant a 'chuck wallah'. Wallah is Anglo-Indian, as in 'box-wallah'.
explanation.definitionFit: The chuckwalla is a big, heavy iguana of the deserts of the south-western US and Mexico.

clue.text: Straight ticket without mark of approval stops man in the lead

indicators.note: without means lacking, so letters spelling the approval mark are taken away
a stopper sits inside a bottle's neck, so these letters go inside the man

blocks.note: taken as written
a tick is the mark a teacher puts by a right answer
the hero is the leading man in a story

explanation.surface: A voter backs a party's whole ticket without approving it, blocking the frontrunner.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters T, I, C and K are struck out of ticket where they fall, leaving T and E; a 'straight ticket' in US politics is a vote for one party's entire list.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight is slang for heterosexual, and hetero is the clipped colloquial form of that word.

clue.text: US department store sent round one fresh cut mulberry tree that Luke mentioned

indicators.note: sending something round turns it to face the other way, so the store's name runs backwards
cut means trimmed, so the final letter is lopped off

blocks.note: Macy's is the famous New York department store
I is the Roman numeral for one
fresh means new

explanation.surface: A New York store dispatches a newly pruned biblical tree.
explanation.definitionFit: In the King James Bible, Luke 17:6 speaks of faith able to uproot the sycamine tree, usually taken to be the black mulberry.

clue.text: Fabrication needing injection of yen with African capital

indicators.note: an injection puts something inside, so the next pieces go into the fabrication

blocks.note: a lie is a made-up story
to yen for something is to long for it
W is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: A false story needs a shot of Japanese money to go with an African city.
explanation.walkthrough: Yen looks like the currency but is the verb for craving.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilongwe is the capital city of Malawi in south-eastern Africa.

clue.text: Wedge-shaped copper centre in juicer stays clean

indicators.note: the centre is the very middle, so only the middle two letters of the kitchen gadget count
stays here are corset supports, which hold the body in, so the outer pieces hold the next one

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
neat as in clean and tidy
the two middle letters of juicer

explanation.surface: A copper-cored juicer is kept spotless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stays' looks like a verb meaning remains; it works as the holding device, with the copper and the juicer's centre on either side.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuneatic means cuneate, wedge-like in shape, from the Latin cuneus for a wedge.

clue.text: Incompetent person’s decline in ecological role, with no end in sight

indicators.note: in places the decline inside the ecological role
no end in sight means the last letter cannot be seen, so it is dropped

blocks.note: to ebb is to decline or fall away
a niche is the role a species fills in its ecosystem

explanation.surface: A hopeless person's role in the ecosystem keeps shrinking with no end in view.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebbich is a variant spelling of nebbish, the Yiddish-derived word for a timid, ineffectual nobody.

clue.text: Local hack has folios seized by member for Hull

indicators.note: something seized is held tight, so these letters are gripped inside the next piece

blocks.note: ff. is the abbreviation for folios, pages
the keel is the backbone member of a ship's hull

explanation.surface: A local journalist's papers are seized by the city of Hull's MP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member for Hull' reads as a Member of Parliament, but Hull is a ship's hull; Hull is a city in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Keffel is a dialect word for a horse, especially an old nag, and a hack is a riding horse.

clue.text: Female with simple bomb carried by published US feminist

indicators.note: what is carried is held inside, so the bomb goes into the next piece

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
an IED is an improvised explosive device, a homemade bomb
a paper that ran a story published it

explanation.surface: A woman with a crude bomb is reported by an American feminist publication.
explanation.definitionFit: Betty Friedan wrote The Feminine Mystique (1963) and co-founded the National Organization for Women.

clue.text: Both endless food and larva?

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the final letter goes from each word
both means the two of them, so the two shortened words are set side by side

blocks.note: grub is slang for food
a grub is an insect larva

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what is at once a meal and an insect grub.
explanation.walkthrough: One word, grub, serves both meanings; trimmed and doubled it gives the answer, and the whole clue describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The grugru is the edible grub of a palm weevil, eaten as a delicacy in the tropics: both food and a larva.

clue.text: A lot of connected pages are taken from cave to return

indicators.note: taken from means removed from, so the first word's letters come out of the second
returning means going back the way you came, so what remains runs backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
cave, Latin for beware, was the schoolboy's warning that a teacher was coming

explanation.surface: Many linked pages are carried out of a cave so they can be brought back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cave' looks like a hollow in rock but is the Latin warning, pronounced KAY-vee.
explanation.definitionFit: The web, the World Wide Web, is a vast collection of pages joined by hyperlinks.

clue.text: Heedlessness of diversion when cycling by lake

indicators.note: cycling means going round, so the first letter moves round to the end

blocks.note: a detour is a diversion from the usual route
Lake Erie, one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Carelessness of taking a detour on a bike ride beside a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Étourderie is French for thoughtlessness or a careless blunder, used in English as a borrowed word.

clue.text: Scott’s boring covers for telephone directory

indicators.note: covers are the outside of a book, so only the outer letters of each word count

blocks.note: the first and last letters of telephone
the first and last letters of directory

explanation.surface: Sir Walter Scott finds the covers of a phone book dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedy is an old form of tedious, found in Sir Walter Scott, so a tiresome thing in his usage.

clue.text: Industrial city left to change course suddenly after setback for turnover, say

indicators.note: a setback sets things back, so the pastry word runs backwards

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
a turnover is a kind of folded pie, so 'say' marks an example
to zig is to make a sharp turn, as in zigzag

explanation.surface: Business news: an industrial city's firm swerves after a fall in turnover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turnover' wants to be company sales, which suits 'setback'; here it is the folded pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: Leipzig is a major manufacturing and trading city in Saxony, eastern Germany.

clue.text: Third of sugar’s to sift on surface for baking

indicators.note: third of means the letter in third place in the word that follows

blocks.note: the third letter of sugar
a riddle is a coarse sieve, and to riddle is to sift

explanation.surface: A baking instruction: a portion of sugar should be sieved over the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surface' looks like a kitchen worktop; it is the flat iron plate on which scones are baked.
explanation.definitionFit: A griddle is a flat iron plate heated for baking scones, pancakes and oatcakes.

clue.text: Ace attempt to make pasty

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards
a shy is a throw or attempt, as at a coconut shy

explanation.surface: A crack attempt at making a Cornish pasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pasty' wants to be the pie; it is the adjective for pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashy means ash-coloured, pale grey, so it describes a wan, pallid complexion.

clue.text: Outwardly and fully visible, looker caught in New York is not seeing state

indicators.note: outwardly means on the outside only, so just the first and last letters of the looker count
fully visible says that the second time every letter is on show, not just the outside
something caught in a place is held inside it, so the cricket letter sits inside the city

blocks.note: a looker is a cutie, an attractive person; its first and last letters
the same looker, now with every letter showing
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
NY is the abbreviation for New York

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a visible beauty caught in New York is in a state of not seeing.
explanation.walkthrough: The one word looker is used twice: once with only its outside showing, then in full.
explanation.definitionFit: Cecutiency is a tendency to blindness or partial loss of sight, from the Latin caecutire, to be blind.
